convoLines.text: "I'm sorry — I'm feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. Can you do anything?"
"The cut's gone hot and it's spreading — I can feel it moving. Clean it out, wrap it tight, please. Before it turns."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
The ground remembers.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll just stop asking.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
"Rest when you can. We'll talk again soon."
"Forget I asked. I'll figure it out."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"This wound — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"The water goes glass-still. That's the The Living Wire telling you it's about to move. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
"This one — Maracujá (Passion Fruit). Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
Another pass over the same ground. Somebody's being careful. Careful people leave cleaner trails — and cleaner trails are still trails.
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
Their voice loosens. The guardedness thins.
"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
Counted.
"Alright. Catch you later."
"Okay. I'll manage on my own."
"This wound — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"an old trapline — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Andres always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"I keep turning over the last thing Andres said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"The fire feels smaller without Andres. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them American Ginseng — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Anyway — I should get going."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Actually, forget it."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We gave them a good burial. Doesn't feel like enough, does it?"
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Ruby shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
"Sorry — I got lost in it for a second. What did you want to ask?"
"I dreamed Andres was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Okay — I need to move. But I'm glad we talked."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"About this wound — I hate to ask twice, but it's still open. Will you?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
As I said — Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The Informant. They just... took Nikos and Ruby. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"I should get back to it."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? I don't actually know how to swim and I'm terrified someone will find out."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"

"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took me. The Informant — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
"We'll see what the treeline brings. We always do."
"Still on what's been happening."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
You show them American Ginseng — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."

deathBeat: d10: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Harold Leone is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d10: 🕯️ Harold Leone is dead — a hushwolf. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
recoverHome: d11: That night, they bring Harold home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d10: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d10: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."
d10: ◈ SYSTEM: "Ooh. NEIGHBORS. You know what neighbors are for? STORYLINES. Go knock — worst case, it's CONTENT. Best case? The show gets BIGGER."
d10: SYSTEM: Naming things. Very human. The audience approves.
d11: SYSTEM: Catalogued. The Codex grows teeth.
d11: SYSTEM: "Organic units require fuel. Noting. Noting loudly. The audience is very quiet, which for them is screaming."
d12: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 37. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 3."
d12: SYSTEM: Naming things. Very human. The audience approves.
burialWindowSay: d11: That night, they bring Harold home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d13: You say a few words for Harold. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d13: You bury Harold. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
d13: ◈ CRISIS — THE FIRST GRAVE. Teresita is dead. The village digs its first grave, and everyone understands at once: this place can kill you. It just did.
